summary: Reviewed and tested the GitHub Actions -> AWS Lightsail deploy pipeline without calling real AWS. (1) Workflow: actionlint 1.7.7 reports no problems. A YAML-level pytest confirms: the only trigger is workflow_dispatch; top-level permissions are contents:read; id-token:write is set only on the deploy job; deploy has needs: tests and if: refs/heads/main; there is no approval environment; build uses linux/amd64 with load:true; the smoke test, the OIDC sign-in and the deploy step run in the right order; role-to-assume comes from secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN with no access keys; the live check runs with --no-run. The 'Check settings' script, run for real, prints '::error::Missing repository variable or secret: X' for each missing setting, exits 1, and exits 0 when all are set. (2) The research suite passes exactly as CI runs it (cd qem-bench && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q, exit 0). It also passes in a copy that holds only the git-tracked and non-ignored files, as a fresh CI checkout would. (3) Smoke test against a production-like server: a fresh Python 3.11 venv with ONLY requirements.prod.txt installed (no matplotlib or seaborn), the image directory layout copied to /tmp/srv (backend, qem-bench src/scripts/configs, frontend_build), and a yarn build with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL='' (the bundle uses relative /api). Port 8123, throwaway DB TEST_smoke_t1, password containing a quote. Full mode passed (the run completed in about 2.7s), --no-run passed, and a wrong password exited 1. I also checked GridFS persistence: I completed a run, restarted the server with an empty QEM_RUNS_DIR, and the run still served conditions (6) and tests (4) from GridFS. The SPA fallback works, unknown /api/* returns a JSON 404, and path traversal is blocked. The throwaway DB was dropped, the server was killed, and the temp files were removed. test_database and supervisor were not touched. (4) deploy.sh release with a stub aws on PATH: when the service is missing it calls create-container-service (medium, scale 1), then push-container-image --label app, then the deployment. The rendered JSON has image ':TEST-qem.app.latest', port 8000/HTTP, health check /api/health, and exactly the 5 env vars, with a password containing quotes, backslash, $, backticks and spaces round-tripped correctly. url=... is written to GITHUB_OUTPUT, the step summary is written, and the temp file is removed by the trap. An existing service skips create. Each of the 8 required settings, when missing, gives a non-zero exit before any aws call. FAILED in cur or next exits non-zero and prints the container log. ONE BUG: if the deployment never reaches ACTIVE, the wait loop runs out and the script still reports success. (5) setup-github-oidc.sh with a stub aws: bash -n is OK. The trust policy has aud sts.amazonaws.com and sub repo:<owner>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/<branch>. A second run skips the provider and role creation and updates the trust policy. The inline policy is lightsail:*, the ARN is printed, and the missing-argument usage error works. (6) The docs match the workflow: secret and variable names, section numbers and cross-references are correct, and section 9.4 uses the GitHub variable CORS_ORIGINS. (7) Preview regression: /api/health ok, /api/qem/overview ok, /api/runs lists 3 runs, test_qem_viewer_api.py 21/21, and the Run Simulations tab shows the 3 previous runs and a run detail with no console errors.

minor.issue: If the 60x15s loop runs out (nextDeployment still DEPLOYING or ACTIVATING, or currentDeployment None), the script falls through and reports success. It prints 'Live at', writes url= to GITHUB_OUTPUT and 'Deployed to' to the summary, then the live check runs against whatever version is serving, possibly the OLD one, and the workflow goes green. Reproduced with a stubbed aws and sleep (test_release_wait_timeout_exits_nonzero FAILS). Fix: track success with a flag and run `exit 1` after the loop if it was not reached. Do the same for the service-ready loop (lines 36-39), which also continues silently after 20 minutes.

Success means next == None and cur == ACTIVE. It does not check that currentDeployment.version is the version just created. If Lightsail clears nextDeployment after a failed rollout while the previous version stays ACTIVE, a failed deploy is reported as success. Suggestion: read containerService.nextDeployment.version from the create-container-service-deployment output (it is currently sent to /dev/null) and wait until currentDeployment.version equals it and is ACTIVE.
Any get-container-services error (expired creds, AccessDenied, throttling) counts as MISSING and triggers create-container-service. It then fails with a less clear error. Low impact.

action_items: deploy.sh: exit non-zero when the deployment wait loop (and the service-ready loop) runs out instead of reporting success. Rerun: cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=... pytest tests/test_deploy_scripts.py -n 0 (test_release_wait_timeout_exits_nonzero must pass)
deploy.sh (recommended): confirm that currentDeployment.version equals the version just created before declaring success
Workflow (recommended): use `uv sync --locked --extra dev` so CI fails if uv.lock is out of date instead of re-resolving silently
critical_code_review_comments: Docker build was NOT verified (no docker in the pod). The image's Python deps were verified instead: requirements.prod.txt resolves and installs on py3.11 aarch64, and the full simulation and analysis subprocess runs with ONLY those packages (no matplotlib or seaborn needed). yarn install --frozen-lockfile under node:20 was not verified; the local build used node 24.

DEPLOY_AWS_LIGHTSAIL.md section 0 says raw per-shot Parquet files are deleted. runs.py keeps raw_runs/*/raw and the parquet files under QEM_RUNS_DIR (about 280 KB per tiny run) until the container is replaced. Soft-deleted runs also keep their GridFS files in Atlas (M0 is 512 MB). Either prune them or reword the doc.

runs._watch: if _store (GridFS upload to Atlas) raises, for example on a transient network error, the run stays 'running' and blocks all new runs until a restart. This was noted in iteration 2 and matters more now that storage is remote. Wrap it in try/except and mark the run failed.
When the smoke test fails on a wrong password it prints a Python JSONDecodeError traceback rather than a clear message. The exit code is correct (1). Cosmetic.

uvicorn runs with --forwarded-allow-ips '*' and the per-IP lockout trusts X-Forwarded-For. The global 20-fail counter in auth.py covers the spoofing case. Each live check adds 1 global failure (the deliberate wrong-password probe), which is acceptable.
The '/api' path without a trailing slash falls through to the SPA's index.html (200 text/html) instead of a 404. Trivial.

success_rate.backend: 95% (20/21 deploy-tooling tests; the 1 failure is the real wait-timeout bug). Research suite passed. Smoke test passed in full and --no-run modes and failed correctly on a wrong password. Viewer API regression 21/21

test_credentials: Owner password from /app/memory/test_credentials.md was not needed for mutations; preview only read. The throwaway server used its own password.
seed_data_creation: None on preview. Throwaway DB TEST_smoke_t1 (local mongo) held the runs created by 2 smoke runs and 1 TEST_persist run. It was dropped afterwards; remaining DBs are admin/config/local/test_database.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run test_deploy_scripts.py with -n 0 and REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL exported (the stub's live URL is the preview /api/health). The tests stub `aws` (and `sleep` for the timeout test) on PATH, so no real AWS calls are made. Production-like smoke recipe: create a uv venv with requirements.prod.txt only; copy backend/*.py, viewer_data, qem-bench/{pyproject,src,scripts,configs} and a yarn build (BUILD_PATH=/tmp/x REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL='') into /tmp/srv/{backend,qem-bench,frontend_build}; start uvicorn with setsid (...) & in a subshell, otherwise the tool call hangs; use a port other than 8001/3000; drop the throwaway DB afterwards. actionlint arm64 binary: /tmp/actionlint.
